feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level CV with clear positioning in digital communications/strategy and credible progression at NACo. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with some missed opportunities to sharpen results and streamline overlapping sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear professional brand: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong digital strategy/communications leadership profile.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions within the same organization signal trust, growth, and increasing scope.  
- Good use of specifics: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add impact and credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more quantified business/organizational results would increase impact.  
- Tighten writing and consistency: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience” (missing “of”); keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs later lists without it); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—consider “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding leadership in digital transformation would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: enterprise web modernization, cross-channel strategy, and systems/workflow design for mission-driven organizations.
- Add a clearer seniority signal by emphasizing leadership of digital programs rather than listing channels first.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel programs across web, email, social media, content, and multimedia. Brings deep expertise in enterprise web modernization, editorial workflow design, and digital systems that strengthen communications in complex, mission-driven organizations. Experienced in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, audience-focused content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid overloading the intro with platform/channel lists already detailed elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Digital strategy & transformation” → “Enterprise digital strategy”; “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Reduce overlap with other sections by focusing this block on capability areas, not tools or soft skills.
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent style throughout.

Suggested rewrite:
Enterprise digital strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS and web platform administration • Editorial systems and governance • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • Workflow architecture and process improvement • Stakeholder and cross-functional coordination • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills almost exactly.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “multimedia,” and “workflow/systems” are already covered in Topline Skills and the header summary.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Make it more outcome-led and anchor it to 3–4 highest-value contributions.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact areas: digital operations/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, governance, and AI search.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams enabled, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten phrasing. Example bullets:
- Built Drupal microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits for major campaigns.
- Improved communications workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet shorter here.
- Governance/analytics/web improvement also echo the summary and prior NACo role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and the most senior-level achievements without repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullet into a sharper outcome line: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make analytics/governance more results-oriented: add adoption, reporting speed, decision-making, or workflow efficiency metrics if available.
- Reframe video studio bullet to show business value: e.g., reduced vendor reliance, increased production volume, or expanded advocacy/event coverage.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; either cut it or add stronger outcomes.
- “Publishing standards and cross-department planning” is close to earlier editorial coordination language; keep this version focused on enterprise governance.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than achievements. Tighten it to emphasize what changed under your leadership and quantify outputs where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + outcome: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Combine newsletter/video bullets and add metrics if available: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and stakeholders, and produced a weekly advocacy video series that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Make cross-functional impact more active: “Built tighter editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving alignment and publishing cadence.”
- Replace “helped improve” with a stronger result: “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with both the earlier Digital Media Manager role and the Recent Projects section.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” also appears in the Director of Digital Media entry; differentiate this role as execution/scale-up rather than governance leadership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Enterprise digital strategy

- Audience-focused content planning

Suggested edit:

- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations at scale
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design

- If space allows, make one bullet outcome-oriented, e.g. “Content operations for high-volume platforms serving 3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize recent strengths tied to current/most recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Put Drupal first and de-emphasize older/less central platforms unless they are current selling points; consider dropping either SharePoint or Power Pages if space is tight.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with a more outcome-oriented phrase like “Airtable-based workflow systems” or “operational workflow systems.”
- If possible, add one impact cue in adjacent sections rather than here, such as “supporting 10,000+ pages” or “50+ publishers,” since skills sections work best when concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating all three verbatim.

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal (enterprise, primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers: **Drupal (migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress (site administration) • SharePoint (intranet/content management) • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**

- If you want more impact, replace weaker tools with proficiency framing: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint; Additional platforms: Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the fuller version in one place and make the other shorter.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless you add platform-specific context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Front-End & Technical Implementation** to distinguish it from platform/CMS skills.
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **JavaScript • HTML5 • CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • jQuery**
- Consider trimming older tech if space is tight: move **jQuery** to the end or remove it unless it is still actively used in current Drupal work.
- If format allows, add light proficiency/context instead of pure listing, e.g. **JavaScript, HTML/CSS, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions** for front-end delivery, tagging, edge logic, and deployment workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- “Technical Implementation” also partially overlaps with automation tools in the separate **Automation & Workflow Systems** section.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add light qualifiers only where defensible, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation)**
- Consider trimming weaker/older overlap tools if not central to recent work; prioritize platforms tied to current consulting and NACo systems leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- **Airtable systems** and **Workflow automation** already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if you actively used them to run cross-team communications workflows

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform breadth and avoid implying deep expertise in all three unless supported.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a qualifier for depth: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys (current) • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows elsewhere, connect to use case rather than tools alone: **Email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, and audience engagement platforms**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid broader engagement wording unless tied to specific platforms.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and separate scope from outcomes: “Improved workflows across web, email, social and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- Add measurable detail where possible: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social support volume, or size/timing of the website refresh.
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating governance/strategy language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast…”
- Replace generic phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with clearer scope and support function.
- Split into 2 concise bullets; emphasize ownership verbs: launched, managed, supported, produced.
- If possible, add outcomes: number of episodes, audience/listens, internal stakeholders supported, or types of policy/program outputs.

Suggested edit
- Supported county innovation and research initiatives that informed NACo programmatic and policy work.
- Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, planning, scripting, recording coordination and production; also produced digital and multimedia content supporting organizational communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on the podcast launch and innovation/research support.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here since stronger, more recent evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
